title: tests/schc main.c: non-IPv6 rule255 decompress assertion passes vacuously via ceiling check
description: Found during ilye.5 codereview (edge pass, worker after reviewer timeouts). In lichen/tests/schc/main.c test_reject_non_ipv6_input, the call lichen_schc_decompress(comp_buf, n, decomp_buf, sizeof(decomp_buf)) passes the NEGATIVE compress error code (n, e.g. -15) as data_len (size_t) — so the profile ceiling check (data_len > SCHC_FRAGMENT_MAX_PACKET_SIZE) rejects it before the rule255 payload validator ever runs. The assertion passes, but not for the reason the comment claims ('Rule 255 RX validates the payload as a complete IPv6 packet...'). Fix: feed an actual non-IPv6 rule255 wire, e.g. bytes {0xff, 0xde, 0xad, 0xbe, 0xef} with len 5, expect rejection from validate_ipv6_transport_lengths (SCHC_ERR_NO_MATCHING_RULE family) — that makes the assertion exercise the profile validate_payload hook it documents. Real RX payload rejection is already covered at parity level (rule255_dual_defect_*_malformed vectors), so this is test-precision cleanup only, P3.
